grapht.caption: Fig. 2 · GraphT, public beta.
grapht.problem: Task apps fix how many levels you can break a project into and never show how tasks connect to each other. With ADHD, not seeing the whole path is what paralyzes you. Notion wasn't enough.
grapht.decision: Tasks as a graph in Neo4j, endlessly divisible and tied to life areas that give every step its context. Clean Architecture on the backend and the frontend.
grapht.imageAlt: GraphT Workbench: a graph of connected tasks next to the inspector of the selected task.

method.label: How I work
method.order: In that order. My rule against analysis paralysis: first I make it work, then I make it right, and only at the end do I get to optimize it.
method.domain: Before all of that comes the domain: I adapt to the business, not the business to me. If the tool I need isn't in my toolbox, I learn it from the fundamentals.

business.question: Does your business run on spreadsheets?
business.pitch: There are probably processes you can automate without throwing away what already works. First I sit down with you to understand how you work; then I tell you what's worth automating and what isn't.

about.label: About me
about.headline: I started by taking toys apart to see how each piece made the whole thing work.
about.quote: “I may not know everything, but I'm open to learning whatever it takes to solve the problem.”
about.beginnings: Around twelve I wanted to make cheats for online games, and someone told me I had to learn to program first; that's why I chose programming at a technical high school. I couldn't go to university. At twenty I started working as a developer at a friend's startup and found out that something I was good at was useful to someone else.
about.grapht: At twenty-two, in a remote job with no structure, ADHD made me lose track of too many tasks. I built my own system so I wouldn't lose them; that's how GraphT was born, and with it the habit of doing things right: domain, clean architecture, tests. Today I bring that same mindset to other people's businesses: understand how they work before writing a single line.
about.outside: Outside of code I like fixing things and learning for the sheer joy of learning.
